investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, so pods remained stuck unscheduled for 120–144 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completed, and the eval produced an empty evidence object — violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in check-expectations.json line 256. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval.

This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-07-19 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no agent VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence, causing a total contract gap across all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote-agent pod times out unscheduled. This is a cluster-level infrastructure resource exhaustion, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) which triggers pod creation; because the pod never starts, no runtime response is returned, and all five required evidence fields remain missing.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has no remaining VM slots for new peer-pod workloads, causing every remote-agent pod to remain Pending until the eval timeout fires.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules at all, leaving only 2 nodes eligible; if those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., existing agents not cleaned up, leaked pods, or quota reduction), the pool is fully saturated.

Tertiary — peer-pod resource leak from a prior eval run or production workload: if previous remote-agent pods were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs may not have completed), their reserved kata.peerpods.io/vm slots could still be held, starving new scheduling attempts.
Lower confidence — node affinity selector change that reduced the eligible node pool from more than 2 to exactly 2 nodes, making the cluster more sensitive to any VM slot consumption.
